content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"'Virgin' symbolizes purity, chastity, and exclusive covenant fidelity to God, corporately picturing God's people (virgin Israel/Zion; the Church as pure bride betrothed to Christ), free from the spiritual adultery of idolatry; secondary registers include Mary's literal virginity, ascetic celibacy, and eschatological readiness (Matt 25).","book_summary":"'Virgin' means the espoused — one betrothed to one husband with the wedding still future. The emphasis is legal-covenantal standing, not moral attainment: the law counts a betrothed virgin already a wife; 'the virgin of Israel' names the ten-tribe house re-espoused after her divorce; virgins in the plural are the bride's companions who follow her in; the whole stands opposite the harlot who goes after many.","consensus_core_identification":"A symbol of purity and undivided faithfulness: God's people as a pure bride pledged to God/Christ, uncorrupted by spiritual adultery.","book_core_identification":"The betrothed party in a covenant marriage — espoused status prior to the wedding, counted legally as wife — applied to re-espoused Israel and (in the plural) to the bride's attendant companions, opposed to the harlot.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION","boundary_disagreement":"The book keeps the marital-covenant referent but shifts the defining feature from moral/spiritual purity (an attainment or quality) to betrothal standing (a legal-covenantal status). It further narrows 'virgin of Israel' to the ten-tribe northern house re-espoused after divorce, and reclassifies plural 'virgins' (Ps 45:14-15; Matt 25:1) as the bride's companions rather than the bride or believers generically — a distinction the consensus does not draw. The consensus's non-bridal registers (Marian literal virginity, ascetic celibacy) are dropped entirely.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"Both readings center on the same category: covenant marriage imagery in which God's people stand as a virgin espoused to one husband, opposed to spiritual harlotry (2 Cor 11:2 is central to both). This rules out DIVERGENT and NOVEL. But the book materially changes the boundary and precision: (1) the essence is redefined from purity-as-quality to espousal-as-status ('covenant standing, not attainment'), grounded in Deut 22:23-24 where the betrothed virgin is legally a wife; (2) 'virgin of Israel' is specified as the divorced-and-re-espoused ten-tribe house, a claim no consensus response makes; (3) plural virgins are systematically distinguished from the bride as her attending companions, reclassifying the Matt 25 virgins whom the consensus treats as professing believers/the bride community. These are substantive boundary changes within an intact referent, i.e., REFINED.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue MATCH: the consensus already frames 'virgin' as a betrothal metaphor (2 Cor 11:2 'betrothed to one husband'; brides awaiting the Bridegroom), so 'espoused' merely restates the bride motif, and the companion/ten-tribe details are immaterial elaboration rather than real boundary disagreement. Conversely, one might press for DIVERGENT on the ground that 'covenant standing, not attainment' rejects the consensus's core of purity as the defining feature; but the book still retains chastity-to-one-husband as the operative contrast with the harlot, so the referent is not replaced.","confidence":"high"}
